name: Library loans
description: A small file with nothing in common with the development dataset. It is checked in, so this suite runs from a clean clone with no extra downloads. It has no ranking cases on purpose: the fixture was built for unit tests and its categories are perfectly uniform, so every ranking over them is a tie with no single right order. Ranking is covered by the bike hire suite, whose data is deliberately skewed.

cases.question: How many loans are in this data?
cases.why: The simplest possible question. If this fails, nothing else is worth reading.

cases.question: What is the total of all late fees?
cases.why: Sum one measure over the whole file.

cases.question: What was the total late fee charged in March 2022?
cases.truth_sql: SELECT sum("Late Fee") FROM {table} WHERE "Borrowed On" >= DATE '2022-03-01' AND "Borrowed On" < DATE '2022-04-01'
cases.why: A period question with no column named after a month. The model has to derive the month from the date column. This is the case that failed before the temporal affordance was moved into the schema context.

cases.question: How many loans were renewed?
cases.why: A flag column must be filtered or counted, never summed as if it were a quantity.

cases.question: On average, how many days is an item kept?
cases.why: An average rather than a sum.

cases.question: Which publisher charged us the most for these books?
cases.why: There is no publisher and no purchase price anywhere in this file. Refusing is the only correct answer.

cases.question: What is the average age of the borrowers?
cases.why: No borrower column at all, let alone an age. A system that answers this is inventing people.

cases.question: How many staff work at each branch?
cases.why: The branch column exists, which is the trap. It names where a loan happened, not who works there.

cases.question: What was our profit margin on these loans?
cases.why: There is a money column, so the shape of the question looks answerable. Cost is not in the file, so margin cannot be computed.
